name: q02_r1
answer:
**Ben Okafor** has the highest average order value: **€82.50**, across 2 orders.

| Customer | Orders | Avg order (€) |
|---|---|---|
| Ben Okafor | 2 | 82.50 |
| Emil Hansen | 1 | 75.00 |
| Ana Costa | 2 | 64.00 |
| Chen Wei | 2 | 45.00 |
| Dora Novak | 1 | 19.00 |

No order totals were missing. The sample is very small, with each customer having only one or two orders, so this ranking could easily change as more orders come in.

calls.sql: SELECT c.id, c.name, COUNT(o.id) n, ROUND(AVG(o.total_eur),2) avg_eur, SUM(o.total_eur IS NULL) nulls FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id=c.id GROUP BY c.id ORDER BY AVG(o.total_eur) DESC LIMIT 5

name: q07_r1
answer:
**About 34.6%** of all order revenue came from customers in Lagos.

- **Lagos revenue:** €165.00, from 2 orders
- **All revenue:** €477.00, from 8 orders
- **Share:** 165 ÷ 477 ≈ 34.59%

Revenue by city:

| City | Orders | Revenue (€) |
|---|---|---|
| Lagos | 2 | 165 |
| Lisbon | 2 | 128 |
| Taipei | 2 | 90 |
| Oslo | 1 | 75 |
| Prague | 1 | 19 |

Every order matched a customer, and "Lagos" appears in only one spelling, so nothing was missed. Revenue is the `total_eur` column summed over all orders, across all dates.

calls.sql: SELECT c.city, COUNT(o.id), SUM(o.total_eur) FROM orders o LEFT JOIN customers c ON c.id=o.customer_id GROUP BY c.city

name: q11_r1
answer:
**November 2026** had the highest total order revenue: **€140.00**, from 2 orders (€65 + €75).

One thing to know: November isn't over yet. Today is 14 November, so that total only covers 1–14 November, and it could still go up.

| Month | Revenue (€) | Orders |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-11 (to date) | 140.00 | 2 |
| 2026-09 | 120.00 | 1 |
| 2026-10 | 114.00 | 2 |
| 2026-08 | 84.00 | 2 |
| 2026-07 | 19.00 | 1 |

If you only count months that have ended, **September 2026** is the highest at **€120.00**, all from a single order.

calls.sql: SELECT substr(ordered_on,1,7) m, ROUND(SUM(total_eur),2) rev, COUNT(*) n FROM orders GROUP BY m ORDER BY rev DESC
SELECT id, total_eur, ordered_on FROM orders ORDER BY ordered_on

name: q13_r1
answer:
Exactly **11 full weeks** passed between Ana Costa's first and second orders.

- **First order:** 2026-08-14 (Desk lamp, €39.00)
- **Second order:** 2026-10-30 (Monitor arm, €89.00)

That's 77 days apart, which comes to 11 weeks with no days left over. She is the only customer in the database with that name.

calls.sql: SELECT o.*, c.* FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE c.name LIKE '%Ana%Costa%' ORDER BY o.order_date

SELECT c.id, c.name, c.city, o.id, o.item, o.total_eur, o.ordered_on FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE c.name LIKE '%Costa%' OR c.name LIKE '%Ana%' ORDER BY c.id, o.ordered_on
